documents.unit: Office of the Dean of Students, Honor Code
documents.title: Understanding Generative AI at UNCW
documents.summary: A student-facing Dean of Students page that gives general AI tips for success. It makes each instructor responsible for deciding whether AI is used and tells students to follow the syllabus, disclose and cite AI use, and keep confidential data out of AI tools. It sets no university-wide permission or ban.
documents.stance_why: The page says "Instructors at UNCW have wide discretion in how they may incorporate AI into their course, if at all" and tells students to "Follow the AI guidelines outlined in your syllabus", so it hands the decision to instructors and sets no stance itself.

units.why: Defines generative AI as tools that "create or significantly revise academic work", setting what the guidance covers; a definition, so informs, general phase, P61.
units.anchor: tools that can create or significantly revise academic work

units.why: Says AI tools "can be helpful, but their effectiveness depends on your understanding of both the tool and the subject"; a statement of benefit with a caveat, not a rule, so P87.
units.anchor: These tools can be helpful, but their effectiveness depends on your understanding
units.fit_note: Also says effectiveness depends on the student understanding the subject, a mild accountability point.

units.why: States AI tools "must be used appropriately"; a general expectation of appropriate use with no specific content, so P116.
units.anchor: they also must be used appropriately
units.frag_start: While AI tools can significantly aid

units.why: "It is the responsibility of students to communicate with their instructors about expectations regarding AI use in each course" assigns students the duty to find out each course rules, so P78.
units.anchor: responsibility of students to communicate with their instructors about expectations regarding AI use

units.why: "Instructors at UNCW have wide discretion in how they may incorporate AI into their course, if at all" leaves the decision to instructors, so P04.
units.anchor: Instructors at UNCW have wide discretion in how they may incorporate AI into their course

units.why: "Students must be certain that they are following their instructor’s expectations" binds students to the instructor-set rule; chosen P78 (follow the course rules) rather than P04 because it addresses the student duty.
units.anchor: Students must be certain that they are following their instructor’s expectations

units.why: "Follow the AI guidelines outlined in your syllabus" tells students to follow the syllabus rules, P78; the next clause about variation is a separate unit.
units.anchor: Follow the AI guidelines outlined in your syllabus.

units.why: "These can potentially be different for each individual course you are enrolled in" says rules vary by course, nearest P11 (course rules do not carry over).
units.anchor: These can potentially be different for each individual course
units.fit_note: States variation across courses rather than that permissions do not carry over.

units.why: "If you’re unsure about what’s allowed, ask your instructor" directly matches P10.
units.anchor: If you’re unsure about what’s allowed, ask your instructor.

units.why: "AI tools are great for inspiring ideas, exploring topics, and examining problems" permits and encourages brainstorming and exploration, so P15.
units.anchor: AI tools are great for inspiring ideas, exploring topics, and examining problems.

units.why: "should be used to support your thinking, not replace it" keeps the student as primary thinker, P32.
units.anchor: they should be used to support your thinking, not replace it

units.why: "Make sure your work reflects your own understanding" requires submitted work to show the student’s own understanding; P30 rather than P29 because it speaks of understanding.
units.anchor: Make sure your work reflects your own understanding.
units.fit_note: Requires work to reflect understanding but does not say students must explain every line.

units.why: "AI generated outputs are known to potentially have biases, inaccuracies, and can elicit ethical concerns" names bias and ethical concerns; chosen P53 because it names harms, though inaccuracy overlaps P31.
units.anchor: AI generated outputs are known to potentially have biases, inaccuracies, and can elicit ethical concerns.
units.fit_note: Also notes inaccuracies (P31) but gives no instruction to verify.

units.why: "Use AI generated content in a responsible way" is a general call to responsible use with no specific content, P116.
units.anchor: Use AI generated content in a responsible way.

units.why: "Be transparent and open about how you are using AI generated content" requires openness about AI use; with the later sentence naming disclosure it is P24.
units.anchor: Be transparent and open about how you are using AI generated content.

units.why: "Properly document its use as necessary" asks students to document AI use where needed, P24.
units.anchor: Properly document its use as necessary.

units.why: "You are expected to disclose, explain, and cite any AI assistance in your work" is the core disclosure rule, P24; the standards clause names citation format but not tool or prompt detail.
units.anchor: You are expected to disclose, explain, and cite any AI assistance in your work
units.fit_note: Names APA, MLA or course guidelines as the citation standard.

units.why: "Never input personal or confidential information into generative AI tools" is a data-protection prohibition, P50.
units.anchor: Never input personal or confidential information into generative AI tools.

units.why: "there’s always a risk of data breaches or unauthorized access" explains why confidential data should not be entered; informs, P50.
units.anchor: there’s always a risk of data breaches or unauthorized access

units.why: Points students to the "AI Hub" for the latest UNCW AI information, directing readers to further guidance, P115.
units.anchor: what’s happening at UNCW regarding AI please check out the

units.why: Lists the Writing Center, Writing Lab and tutoring as help for students struggling academically, sending students to human support; P72.
units.anchor: students who may be struggling with a variety of academic related issues
units.fit_note: Not AI-specific; general academic support listing.

notes: Single university-layer page; AI section is a short list of five tips. The writing/tutoring resources unit is not AI-specific. No school, computing or course documents included.
